headline: Shore Line East adds four weekday trains as new schedule begins
dek: The expanded CTrail schedule adds afternoon and evening trips between New Haven and New London, including a connection for riders arriving from New York.
body: CTrail Shore Line East’s expanded weekday schedule began Monday, adding four trains between New Haven and New London and shortening some of the long gaps that have shaped travel along Connecticut’s shoreline. The change affects commuters and other riders using stations from New Haven to southeastern Connecticut, with new afternoon and evening options in both directions.

The new schedule adds two eastbound trains from New Haven Union Station to New London. Train 1628 leaves at 2:55 p.m. and reaches New London at 4:05 p.m.; train 1640 leaves at 6:03 p.m. and arrives at 7:13 p.m., according to the [official Shore Line East schedule effective Oct. 5](https://shorelineeast.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SLE-October-5th-schedule_edit.pdf). Both trains serve the line’s stations, including Branford, Guilford, Madison, Clinton, Westbrook and Old Saybrook.

Two new westbound trains fill part of the return-trip gap. Train 1683 departs New London at 4:40 p.m. and reaches New Haven Union Station at 5:49 p.m. Train 1693 leaves New London at 7:28 p.m. and arrives in New Haven at 8:37 p.m. The official timetable also shows several existing trains with adjusted numbers or times, so a rider who remembers an older departure should check the current schedule rather than rely on the previous timetable.

The 6:03 p.m. eastbound trip is especially relevant to passengers connecting from the New Haven Line. The new timetable lists a connection from Metro-North Super Express Train 3542, which leaves New York’s Grand Central Terminal at 4:11 p.m. and Stamford at 4:55 p.m. before reaching New Haven. Connecticut officials had described the connection as a way to make an evening trip toward the shoreline more practical, but the state’s schedule warns that connecting-service times are not guaranteed.

The service increase follows an additional $3 million for the Connecticut Department of Transportation in budget adjustments approved during the 2026 legislative session, according to [Gov. Ned Lamont’s announcement](https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/09-2026/governor-lamont-announces-additional-shore-line-east-rail-service-coming-on-october-5). The governor’s office said the schedule was shaped by customer-satisfaction survey responses and feedback to train and customer-service staff. The goal was to target periods when riders had fewer choices, not to redesign the line’s route or add new stations.

The expansion is meaningful because Shore Line East remains below its pre-pandemic service and ridership levels. The [New Haven Register reported](https://www.nhregister.com/connecticut/article/ct-shore-line-east-more-trains-amtrak-22422965.php) that the four additions bring the line to 24 weekday trains, compared with 36 before the pandemic, and that ridership was about 247,000 last year versus roughly 660,000 in 2019. Those figures provide context for the change: the new trips improve the timetable without restoring the line to its earlier frequency.

Shore Line East connects New Haven with New London and stops at State Street and Union Station in New Haven, as well as Branford, Guilford, Madison, Clinton, Westbrook, Old Saybrook and New London. The corridor serves shoreline communities that rely on rail for work, school, medical appointments and connections to the broader New Haven and New York markets. The added evening departures may be most useful to people whose schedules do not fit the older midday gaps or the limited late-day choices.

The line’s operator says passengers should use the interactive trip planner or current timetable before traveling, particularly when connecting to Metro-North or Amtrak. The published schedule notes that Amtrak trains listed for Shore Line East accept only a CTrail monthly pass or ten-trip ticket, and passengers must reserve a seat through Amtrak’s RideReserve program. The immediate test for the expansion will be whether the new trips make those connection windows dependable enough to bring more riders back to the corridor.
author: NorthEast News Desk
